title: Recognising SAF personnel and sharing lessons from Middle East repatriation flights
asked: Whether the Ministry will consider formally recognising SAF personnel involved in recent repatriation flights from the Middle East, and developing exhibitions or public education initiatives about the choices and personal courage required to organise such efforts from active warzones.
response: The SAF has a framework to recognise units and personnel who took part in operations, and will do the same for the recent mission. Within operational security, it will profile the mission's planning, execution and background training. The mission involved air crew, headquarter planners, intelligence analysts, policy staff, a military medical team, defence partners and Full-time National Servicemen. In a supplementary reply, the Minister said the answer to both questions was yes, and that lessons would be shared with servicemen and the wider public.

key_points.point: The SAF has a framework to recognise units and personnel who have participated in operations.
key_points.speaker: Mr Chan Chun Sing
key_points.quote: the Singapore Armed Forces (SAF) has a framework to recognise all our units and personnel who have participated in operations.

key_points.point: The same recognition will apply to the recent mission.
key_points.speaker: Mr Chan Chun Sing
key_points.quote: We will similarly do so for the recent mission undertaken by the SAF in service of our nation.

key_points.point: Within operational security, the SAF will profile the mission's planning, execution and background training.
key_points.speaker: Mr Chan Chun Sing
key_points.quote: Within the bounds of operational security, the SAF will profile the mission planning, execution and the background training that enabled the SAF to execute this mission.

key_points.point: The mission was enabled by collective efforts across the SAF and other agencies, including beyond MINDEF.
key_points.speaker: Mr Chan Chun Sing
key_points.quote: this mission was made possible by the collective efforts of many across the SAF and other agencies, including those beyond the Ministry of Defence (MINDEF).

key_points.point: The team included air crew, headquarter planners, intelligence analysts and policy staff, some non-uniform officers, who worked at short notice on flight plans, diplomatic clearances and contingency scenarios.
key_points.speaker: Mr Chan Chun Sing
key_points.quote: Besides the air crew who mounted the flights, there was also a team of headquarter planners, intelligence analysts and policy staff, some of whom are non-uniform officers, who worked at short notice to develop a safe flight plan, obtain diplomatic clearances and formulate various contingency scenarios and responses.

key_points.point: A military medical team was deployed for the safety and well-being of those on board.
key_points.speaker: Mr Chan Chun Sing
key_points.quote: We had a military medical team deployed to ensure the safety and well-being of those on board

key_points.point: Commercial personnel from defence partners, including ST Engineering Defence Aviation Services and ST Airport Services, supported aircraft maintenance and cargo management alongside uniform engineers.
key_points.speaker: Mr Chan Chun Sing
key_points.quote: commercial personnel from our defence partners, including ST Engineering Defence Aviation Services and ST Airport Services, deployed alongside our uniform engineers to support aircraft maintenance and cargo management.

key_points.point: Full-time National Servicemen prepared and equipped the aircraft for the two flights.
key_points.speaker: Mr Chan Chun Sing
key_points.quote: Locally, our Full-time National Servicemen ensure that the aircraft was prepared and equipped in a timely manner for the two flights.

key_points.point: In the supplementary reply, the Minister said the answer to both questions was yes.
key_points.speaker: Mr Chan Chun Sing
key_points.quote: The answer to both questions is yes.

key_points.point: The team will be debriefed thoroughly and relevant lessons shared with servicemen, including lessons not made publicly available.
key_points.speaker: Mr Chan Chun Sing
key_points.quote: We intend, like in any operation, to debrief the team thoroughly and then we will share the relevant lessons with our servicemen, including those that may not be made publicly available.

key_points.point: Facets of the work will be shared with the wider public through media, as was done in the first tranche.
key_points.speaker: Mr Chan Chun Sing
key_points.quote: we will certainly do so as we have done so in the first tranche with the media, including our local newspapers and broadcast media, to highlight some of the work that is done behind the scenes to enable this mission.

left_open: Whether a dedicated exhibition will be developed, as distinct from sharing through media.
supplementary: Whether lessons from the mission can be included in training syllabi for commanders and shared with servicemen and the public.
